title: Completed Jacobian homology agrees with completed ordinary conormal homology
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $C$ a finite type commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Write $\widehat C=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}C/I^nC$ for its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Choose a surjective $A$-algebra map $\alpha:Q=A[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\to C$, with $s\geq0$ finite and kernel $K$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Define the $C$-linear map $d_\alpha:K/K^2\to C^{\oplus s}$ by $[f]\mapsto(\alpha(\partial f/\partial y_j))_j$, and put $M_1=\ker d_\alpha$, $M_0=\operatorname{coker}d_\alpha$. For each $i\in\{0,1\}$ let $\widehat M_i=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}M_i/I^nM_i$, a $\widehat C$-module by componentwise multiplication, where $I^nM_i=(I^nC)M_i$. Let $\beta:P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I\to\widehat C$ be any surjective $A$-algebra map, with $r\geq0$ finite and kernel $J$. Define $d_\beta:J/J^2\to\widehat C^{\oplus r}$ by $[f]\mapsto(\beta(\partial f/\partial x_j))_j$, where derivatives on $P$ extend polynomial differentiation continuously for the $I$-adic topology. Then there are $\widehat C$-linear isomorphisms $\widehat M_1\cong\ker d_\beta$ and $\widehat M_0\cong\operatorname{coker}d_\beta$.

source.place: Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), together with presentation independence in Tag 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy); take homology using the flatness/exact completion identified in the proof of 0GAF.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to the finite polynomial algebra $Q$ and to $C$: both are Noetherian. Hence $K$ has finite generators $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Put $N=K/K^2$, $F=C^{\oplus s}$, and $T=\operatorname{im}d_\alpha$. The classes of the $k_i$ generate $N$ over $C$: a coefficient in $Q$ acts through $Q/K=C$, since $K$ annihilates $K/K^2$. Thus $N$ and $F$ are finite $C$-modules. The images of generators of $N$ generate $T$, and images of the coordinate basis generate $M_0=F/T$. Finally $M_1\subseteq N$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. This verifies finiteness of every term in the two short exact sequences used below.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic); finite modules in the proof of restricted.tex Tag 0GAF.

proof.text: The ideal $IC$ is finitely generated because $C$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] to $(C,IC)$: $\widehat C$ is $I\widehat C$-adically complete and $\widehat C/I\widehat C\cong C/IC$ as $C$-algebras. The images of $\alpha(y_1),\ldots,\alpha(y_s)$ generate $C/IC$ over $A/I$: reduce a polynomial expression for any lift in $C$ modulo $I$. Thus $\widehat C/I\widehat C$ is finite type over $A/I$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. These are precisely the completeness and finite-type-modulo-$I$ hypotheses for the completed-presentation independence used in Step 5. The extended ideal generated by $IC$ in $\widehat C$ equals $I\widehat C$, since both are generated by the images of elements of $I$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); restricted.tex Tag 0GAF, first paragraph of its proof.

proof.text: Let $\widehat Q=\varprojlim_nQ/I^nQ$. By [lem-per-polynomial-conormal-completion], the map $\widehat\alpha:\widehat Q\to\widehat C$ is surjective with kernel $K'=K\widehat Q$, and its continuous conormal complex is identified with $(N\otimes_C\widehat C\xrightarrow{d_\alpha\otimes1}F\otimes_C\widehat C)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] over $C$, with ideal $IC$, to the finite modules $N,F$. Its natural comparison identifies this tensor complex with $(\widehat N\xrightarrow{\widehat{d_\alpha}}\widehat F)$. To match the tensor order, use the balanced maps $n\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes n$ and $b\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes b$, which are inverse. The comparison is then $n\otimes b\mapsto b\,\iota_N(n)$; its naturality gives $\widehat{d_\alpha}(b\,\iota_N(n))=b\,\iota_F(d_\alpha n)$. Finally $\widehat F\cong\widehat C^{\oplus s}$ by taking the $s$ coordinates of each compatible sequence, with inverse obtained by assembling those coordinates. This is valid also when $s=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), the completed conormal and differential calculation; algebra.tex Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3).

proof.text: The sequences $0\to M_1\to N\to T\to0$ and $0\to T\to F\to M_0\to0$ are short exact sequences of finite $C$-modules by Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] to each with ideal $IC$. The completed differential factors as the surjection $\widehat N\to\widehat T$ followed by the injection $\widehat T\to\widehat F$, because completion applies a map to each coordinate of a compatible sequence. Therefore its kernel is exactly the image of $\widehat M_1\hookrightarrow\widehat N$, and its image is exactly $\widehat T\subseteq\widehat F$. The second completed sequence identifies $\widehat F/\widehat T$ with $\widehat M_0$. All these maps are $\widehat C$-linear by the cited statement. By Step 3 the kernel and cokernel of the continuous conormal differential for $\widehat\alpha$ are consequently $\widehat M_1$ and $\widehat M_0$.

source.place: Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), part (2), applied to the two finite-module sequences; restricted.tex Tag 0GAF, homology of its complex comparison.

proof.text: Use only the presentation-independence assertion of [lem-per-completed-cotangent-transitivity], applied with both algebras denoted $B,C$ there equal to $\widehat C$ and with their homomorphism the identity. The base ring is the Noetherian ring $A$ and the ideal is $I$; both copies of $\widehat C$ satisfy its completeness and finite-type-modulo-$I$ assumptions by Step 2. For the pair $(A,\widehat C)$, the two presentations are $\widehat\alpha:\widehat Q\twoheadrightarrow\widehat C$ of Step 3 and the given $\beta:P\twoheadrightarrow\widehat C$. Any $A$-algebra map $\beta$ is $I$-adically continuous: it sends $I^nP$ into $I^n\widehat C$ for every $n$, by writing a member of $I^nP$ as a sum of scalar multiples from $I^n$. Thus this includes the arbitrary map allowed in the statement, without an extra continuity hypothesis. The cited node gives $\widehat C$-linear chain maps in both directions between the two conormal complexes, whose composites are chain homotopic to the respective identities. No transitivity exact sequence is used here.

source.place: Tag 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy), statement and proof Steps 1-2; the presentation-independence clause already included in the cited node.

proof.text: For completeness, these homotopy inverses induce inverse maps on both modules at issue. In a two-term complex $L^{-1}\xrightarrow{d}L^0$, a homotopy between an endomorphism $u$ and the identity is a linear $h:L^0\to L^{-1}$ with $u^{-1}-1=hd$ and $u^0-1=dh$. On $\ker d$, the first difference is zero. On $\operatorname{coker}d$, the second difference has image in $\operatorname{im}d$, hence is zero. Chain maps preserve kernels and carry images into images, so they descend to these two modules. Apply this calculation to the two composites from Step 5. Their induced maps are inverse $\widehat C$-linear isomorphisms. Composing with the identifications of Step 4 gives $\widehat M_1\cong\ker d_\beta$ and $\widehat M_0\cong\operatorname{coker}d_\beta$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy), passage from homotopy equivalence to the two homology modules, explicitly computed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q119-5afcb670b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement is unchanged, and it is what Stacks 0GAF/0GAE (restricted.tex) give for homology: B->B^ is flat and the modules are finite. The item allows any A-algebra beta, not only continuous ones; Step 5 shows such a map is automatically continuous (it sends I^nP into I^nC^), so this is not a weakening. Step 1: Noetherianity (00FN) and the submodule node (00IK) make K/K^2, C^s, T, M0 and M1 finite. Step 2: the 05GG node applied to (C, IC) gives completeness and C^/IC^ = C/IC, which are exactly the hypotheses of the transitivity node. Step 3: lem-per-polynomial-conormal-completion, whose finitely-generated-kernel hypothesis comes from Step 1, plus the 00MA tensor node with its naturality clause give (N^ -> F^) with the completed d_alpha; the tensor-swap and coordinate identifications are consistent. Step 4: exact completion (00MB node) on 0->M1->N->T->0 and 0->T->F->M0->0 gives ker = M1^ and coker = M0^, C^-linear. Step 5 uses only the presentation-independence sentence that is in the statement of lem-per-completed-cotangent-transitivity, applied with B = C = C^ and the identity. That node does not say C^-linear explicitly; its complexes are of C^-modules and the source 0GAE says B-modules, so I accept it. Step 6 is a correct elementary homotopy-to-homology argument. Edge cases r=0, s=0, I=0, I=A and C=A/(t-1) all hold. No duplicate: I searched the DAG for 0GAE/0GAF and conormal/cotangent wording and read 6 related nodes; none states this comparison, and the transitivity node does not restate the item. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses; off-unit citations are only Mathlib leaves; the two unsplit cited nodes have no proof_deps, so there is no cycle. No new nodes, no tool_uses, no SGA. The citer lem-per-jacobian-torsion-etale-shrink Step 2 uses exactly the stated isomorphisms.
